content_voiceover: This flowchart covers first line management of marginal zone lymphoma across its four subtypes. For gastric MALT lymphoma, everything hinges on H pylori status and the t eleven eighteen translocation. H pylori positive disease without that translocation gets antibiotic eradication alone, but translocation positive disease needs antibiotics plus involved site radiotherapy, since it typically won't respond to eradication by itself. Non gastric MALT and nodal marginal zone lymphoma are managed more like follicular lymphoma, with radiation for localized stage one or two disease and rituximab based chemoimmunotherapy or observation for advanced stage. Splenic marginal zone lymphoma is distinctive because hepatitis C status matters a great deal. If the patient is hepatitis C positive with splenomegaly, you treat the hepatitis C first, since viral clearance alone can induce lymphoma remission. Asymptomatic splenic disease is simply observed. Across subtypes, rituximab maintenance is common after induction. In the relapsed or refractory setting, options expand to covalent BTK inhibitors like zanubrutinib, PI3K inhibitor copanlisib, lenalidomide combinations, and axicabtagene ciloleucel CAR T cell therapy in later lines. Keep in mind any marginal zone lymphoma subtype can transform to diffuse large B cell lymphoma, and overall management overlaps substantially with follicular lymphoma.
keypoints: Gastric MALT treatment depends on H pylori and t eleven eighteen status
Translocation positive gastric MALT needs radiation, not antibiotics alone
Hepatitis C positive splenic MZL is treated by treating the hepatitis C first
Relapsed disease options include BTK inhibitors and CAR T cell therapy
Any MZL subtype can transform to diffuse large B cell lymphoma
keypoint_voiceover: Remember gastric MALT therapy splits on H pylori and t eleven eighteen status, splenic MZL with hepatitis C gets antiviral treatment first, and relapsed disease now includes BTK inhibitors and CAR T options, with transformation to diffuse large B cell lymphoma always a possibility across subtypes.
